title: Can You Score 80% On This Treatments Quiz?
summary: Recognise treatments, unravel how they work and put your knowledge to the test across five different challenges.

landing.intro:
Know your treatments?
Put your knowledge to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds. Five ways to test your treatment knowledge. Begin with familiar names, explore how treatments work, separate similar terms, spot accurate statements and finish with short descriptive scenarios.

There are six text-only questions per round. Choose one of four answers and the next question appears automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. Your target is 24 correct answers out of 30.

Questions describe treatment names and general principles, not what care an individual needs. A familiar name does not establish effectiveness or suitability. The content was checked against NHS, National Cancer Institute and NCCIH information.

steps: Press Start Quiz, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question. Each round changes the type of challenge, and questions advance automatically.
Complete all five rounds to reveal your score, strongest topic and answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not medical advice, a clinical assessment or a healthcare qualification. Ask a qualified healthcare professional about treatment decisions.

stage-1.preAdCopy: You know the names. Now look behind them.

next.tagline: Go beyond the name to the method.

stage-2.preAdCopy: You have explored the methods. Next, separate the lookalikes.

stage-3.preAdCopy: Three rounds complete. Can you spot a convincing mix-up?

stage-4.preAdCopy: One round left. Put the clues together in short scenarios.

next.tagline: Read the clues and identify the approach.

stage-5.preAdCopy: All 30 answers are in. Reveal your score and see which topics stood out.

profile-1.title: Treatment Trivia Expert
profile-1.copy: You connected treatment names, methods and scenarios with impressive accuracy. That is a strong result on this general-knowledge challenge.

profile-2.title: Therapy-Savvy Thinker
profile-2.copy: You passed this challenge with a good understanding of the treatment names. Review the ones you missed to complete the picture.

profile-3.title: Promising Treatment Spotter
profile-3.copy: You knew more than half of the answers, but a few similar-sounding therapies caught you out.

profile-4.title: Curious Health Learner
profile-4.copy: Some names were familiar; others were harder to place. Your answer review shows which terms you mixed up.

profile-5.title: A Fresh Start
profile-5.copy: Some treatment names were unfamiliar, and that is a useful starting point. Review your missed answers to build your knowledge.

score.passed: You passed the medical treatments challenge!
score.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. Your score reflects your answers to this quiz; it does not assess clinical knowledge or qualify you to provide healthcare.

treatments-r1q1.question: Which treatment uses tailored exercises to help restore movement?

answers.a4: Radiotherapy

treatments-r1q2.question: Which practice involves inserting fine needles at selected points?

answers.a4: Acupuncture

treatments-r1q3.question: What kind of treatment is cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)?

answers.a4: A radiation treatment

treatments-r1q4.question: Which cancer treatment uses medicines to kill cancer cells or stop their growth?

answers.a4: A diagnostic scan

answers.a2: Cups that create suction on the skin
answers.a4: Cups used to collect donated blood

answers.a1: Giving donated blood components through a vein
answers.a2: Filtering waste out of the blood
answers.a3: Measuring blood pressure with a cuff
answers.a4: Removing a blood sample for testing

treatments-r2q1.question: What does dialysis remove from the blood?

answers.a4: Only disease-fighting antibodies

treatments-r2q2.question: What does insulin help the body do?

answers.a4: Turn sound into nerve signals

treatments-r2q3.question: How do antibiotics act against susceptible bacteria?

answers.a2: They remove all bacteria by filtering blood
answers.a3: They teach muscles to resist infection
answers.a4: They kill bacteria or stop them multiplying

treatments-r2q4.question: What does a TENS machine deliver through pads on the skin?

answers.a4: A stream of ultrasound gel

treatments-r2q5.question: In cancer care, what is immunotherapy designed to help do?

answers.a1: Replace the immune system with donor blood
answers.a3: Help the immune system fight cancer
answers.a4: Numb a small area for stitches

answers.a1: Only a small patch of skin becomes numb
answers.a2: The person stays fully alert without medication
answers.a3: The blood is replaced with a saline solution
answers.a4: Medicines make the person unconscious for the procedure

treatments-r3q1.question: Which pairing correctly distinguishes chemotherapy from radiotherapy?

answers.a4: Chemotherapy: surgery; radiotherapy: exercise

treatments-r3q2.question: Despite its name, occupational therapy is not just about jobs. What is its focus?

answers.a4: Teaching medical staff how to operate

treatments-r3q3.question: Ultrasound therapy and radiotherapy sound similar. Which distinction is correct?

answers.a1: Ultrasound uses radiation; radiotherapy uses sound
answers.a2: Ultrasound uses sound; radiotherapy uses radiation
answers.a3: Both use electrical skin pads instead of waves
answers.a4: Both work by filtering the blood

treatments-r3q4.question: How does local anaesthesia differ from general anaesthesia?

answers.a1: Local makes you unconscious; general numbs an area
answers.a2: Local is a talking therapy; general is a medicine
answers.a3: Local replaces blood; general filters blood
answers.a4: Local numbs an area; general makes you unconscious

treatments-r3q5.question: Which pairing correctly describes a vaccine and an antibiotic?

answers.a1: Vaccine: prepares immunity; antibiotic: acts against bacteria
answers.a2: Vaccine: kills all bacteria; antibiotic: prepares immunity
answers.a3: Vaccine: treats fractures; antibiotic: blocks pain signals
answers.a4: Vaccine: filters blood; antibiotic: replaces blood cells

treatments-r3q6.question: Is physiotherapy simply another name for massage?

answers.a1: Yes — every session must consist only of massage
answers.a2: No — it can include exercise, hands-on care and advice
answers.a3: No — it consists only of surgical procedures
answers.a4: Yes — but it is used only by professional athletes

treatments-r4q1.question: Which statement about CBT is accurate?

answers.a1: It replaces all thoughts with positive slogans
answers.a2: It is a medicine that must be injected
answers.a3: It works without any participation from the person
answers.a4: It explores links between thoughts, feelings and actions

treatments-r4q2.question: Which statement about chemotherapy is accurate?

answers.a1: Chemotherapy can only be given through a vein
answers.a2: Some chemotherapy is taken as tablets or capsules
answers.a4: Chemotherapy is another name for radiotherapy

treatments-r4q3.question: Which statement about occupational therapy is accurate?

answers.a1: It is only available to people with paid jobs
answers.a2: It is exclusively a treatment for broken bones
answers.a3: It can support people at home, school or work
answers.a4: It always requires the person to change career

treatments-r4q4.question: Which statement about the evidence for cupping is accurate?

answers.a1: Evidence that it helps pain is limited, not conclusive
answers.a2: Its popularity proves it works for every condition
answers.a3: Skin marks prove a disease has been cured
answers.a4: It has no possible side effects because it is traditional

treatments-r4q5.question: Which statement about cancer radiotherapy is accurate?

answers.a1: It works by replacing all the blood in the body
answers.a2: It is the same as having a routine diagnostic X-ray
answers.a3: It always destroys every cancer cell immediately
answers.a4: It can damage cancer-cell DNA to stop growth or kill cells

treatments-r4q6.question: Which statement about cancer treatment is accurate?

answers.a1: Surgery and medicines can never be combined
answers.a2: Every type of cancer needs exactly the same treatment
answers.a3: A treatment plan may combine several approaches
answers.a4: Only one treatment can ever be used for a person

treatments-r5q1.question: A therapist helps someone practise dressing and adapt everyday tasks after an illness. Which service is described?

answers.a4: Acupuncture

treatments-r5q2.question: A clinician works on swallowing difficulties as part of a specialist therapy service. Which profession fits?

answers.a4: Pharmacy

treatments-r5q3.question: A surgeon uses a blood vessel to create a route around a blocked coronary artery. What is the procedure?

answers.a4: Local anaesthesia

treatments-r5q4.question: A person follows guided exercises in warm water as part of rehabilitation. What is this called?

answers.a4: Cupping

treatments-r5q5.question: A team focuses on symptom relief, comfort and quality of life during a serious life-limiting illness. What care is described?

answers.a4: Palliative care

treatments-r5q6.question: In a structured session, someone examines an unhelpful thought and practises a different response with a therapist. Which approach fits?

answers.a4: General anaesthesia
